episodes.title: Why People Join Cults: Belief and Control with Alan R. Warren
episodes.description:
Why do people join cults—and what happens when belonging depends on never questioning a leader? True crime author and radio host Alan R. Warren returns to The Kino Isaac Podcast to explore belief, manipulation, and the truths we choose to accept.

Drawing on his book Cults: The Interviews, Volume 9, Alan discusses the experiences of cult survivors, the search for acceptance, and why he believes intelligence alone does not protect someone from manipulation. He also explains why understanding children raised inside these groups requires a different perspective from understanding adults who choose to join.

Kino raises a challenging question: where is the line between building an audience and creating a following that discourages independent thought? Their discussion examines disagreement, personal freedom, and what happens when a leader’s authority becomes unquestionable.

The conversation then turns to Alan’s novel The Convenient Truth. Through detective Eddie James, the story explores police corruption, protected reputations, and the consequences of pursuing an easy suspect instead of the truth. Alan reflects on the parallels he sees between the fears of the 1960s and the narratives circulating today.

Watch for a thoughtful conversation about belonging, accountability, and the importance of remaining willing to question what we believe.

KEY TOPICS:

• Why people seek belonging in cults
• Cult survivors and children raised in controlling groups
• The difference between an audience and an unquestioning following
• Disagreement, authority, and independent thought
• Police corruption and moral choices in The Convenient Truth
• Historical fear, social media, and recurring patterns of influence
